description.text: Tommaso Parentucelli, born on 15 November 1397 in Sarzana, rose through the ranks of the Church to become Pope Nicholas V after the death of Eugene IV. He was elected on 6 March 1447 and took the name Nicholas in honour of his early patron, Niccolò Albergati.

During his eight‑year pontificate he sought to make Rome a centre of the Renaissance, restoring aqueducts, rebuilding churches, and commissioning the design of the future Basilica of St. Peter. He also founded a library of five thousand volumes, many of which were rescued from the Turks after the fall of Constantinople.

curiosities.text: Nicholas ordered the restoration of the Aqua Virgo aqueduct, whose basin later became the site of the Trevi Fountain.
He commissioned the architectural plans that would eventually lead to the construction of the Basilica of St. Peter.
The papal library he founded contained five thousand volumes, including manuscripts rescued from the Turks after the fall of Constantinople.
